A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaGA and MG-Geo, with matching core methods and overlapping experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original geolocation evaluations, interactive prompting experiments, training-stage ablations, and expert assessments of generated dialogues.

after.justification: v3 retains original experimental results and adds dataset-component ablations, Introspection and backbone-transfer experiments, and additional benchmark results.

M1.justification: v3 Appendix F introduces GaGA (MP16-Pro), adding retrieval-augmented generation with an external knowledge base. Appendix H also revises the Introspection prompt to require explicit visual-evidence checks and removal of unsupported clues. The base CLIP/Llama3 architecture and two-stage projector/QLoRA training remain substantially unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that existing datasets or experiments were regenerated using the revised prompt.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation on YFCC4k and uses MP16-Pro as an external retrieval corpus. This expands coverage within the existing global image-geolocation task. The OSV-5M and Google Landmarks training sources, GWS15k-style benchmark, OSV-5M-test, Im2GPS3k, and 547-image interactive setting are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership changes substantially. v3 Table 2 replaces the main Qwen-VL row with Qwen2.5-VL and Qwen3-VL, adds GLOBE, and adds coordinate comparisons with GeoReasoner and GRE. Table 6 adds ISNs and RFM S2 on OSV-5M-test. Table 9 adds several Im2GPS3k comparators while dropping PlaNet, CPlaNet, and ISNs there. The GPT-4V human dialogue comparison disappears. Hybrid and PIGEOTTO match the earlier OSV-5M-Baseline and PIGEON rows rather than constituting new comparators.

E3.justification: v2's three-expert, 50-sample dialogue assessment disappears. v3 introduces component ablations using Geoscore, clue hit rates, and LLM/MLLM judging, plus a size-matched Introspection-removal protocol and a Qwen3 transfer-training recipe. These are distinct experimental designs. The GWS15k sampling algorithm and original 547-image Direct/+Q/+QA evaluation are substantially retained, with the latter renamed as interaction tiers.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of ambiguous versus high-specificity cues, five dataset-component combinations, Introspection removal at a fixed training-sample budget, and transfer to Qwen3 (Tables 4, 5, 7, and 8). It also adds geographic error analysis and further qualitative cases. The earlier training-stage ablation survives as Table 13; renaming the existing interaction modes does not itself constitute a new analysis.

E5.justification: The Fleiss' kappa agreement statistics accompanying v2's expert dialogue ratings (Table V) are removed with that study. v3 supplies no corresponding reliability statistic for its automated judges. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: The principal GaGA GWS15k scores, including 63.06% country accuracy, 6.28% city accuracy, and 3113.0 Geoscore, and the base Im2GPS3k row are retained. v3 adds substantial baseline, YFCC4k, retrieval, ablation, and transfer results; for example, the new retrieval variant reports 37.1% Acc@25km on Im2GPS3k. Human ratings, LLaVA-Llama3's +QA results, and several region-level and OSV distance-threshold entries disappear. Clue-frequency findings also change, with the largest category changing from road in v2 Figure 4 to architecture in v3 Figure 8.

T1.justification: v3 Section 5.3 introduces the mathematical definition s(c)=1-H(G|c)/H(G) and a salience-weighted condition characterizing a Similarity Trap together with a localization-error threshold. This is a limited formal addition without a theorem or proof. The newly displayed standard training losses largely explicate the retained training procedure.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain MG-Geo, GaGA, and interactive geolocation. v3 broadens the headline performance claim from GWS15k to multiple benchmarks and adds formal investigation of the Similarity Trap to its stated contributions. These extend the existing contribution claims without replacing the paper's central research objective.

C2.justification: v3 substantially develops the interpretation of cue specificity and interaction failures, including the claim that the Similarity Trap is the primary bottleneck. It acknowledges MG-Geo's long-tailed distribution, possible post-hoc rationalization during Introspection, and limits on comparisons using reproduced GWS15k splits. Conversely, v2's explanation of fine-scale coordinate failures through numerical token prediction and its discussion of additional future modalities are removed.

D1.justification: v3 adds a dataset access link and describes releases of splits, prompts, generation-path tags, reconstruction scripts, and per-country distributions. It newly specifies eight RTX4090 GPUs, a two-layer projector, and transfer-training details. Most original training hyperparameters remain available in Tables 10–11. Some earlier details disappear, including GPT-4V decoding settings and the GeoReasoner adaptation recipe. These are changes in documented access and reproducibility information; actual online availability was not checked.

R1.justification: v3 replaces much of the generic MLLM discussion with a generation-based geolocation survey distinguishing retrieval augmentation from intrinsic reasoning. It adds substantive positioning against Img2Loc, GeoRanker, GLOBE, and GRE, plus a dataset comparison emphasizing expert-guided reasoning and dialogue. Several social/text-geolocation and unrelated domain references disappear. The later G3 citation is a different work from v2's guidebook-grounding G^3.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method explanation, and experimental narrative are extensively rewritten. The dataset section moves before the model section, while prompts, benchmark construction, and retained analyses move into organized appendices. The standalone discussion and biographies disappear, and the title, author presentation, and section conventions change.

P2.justification: The document changes from a two-column journal layout to a single-column conference layout. v3 merges the main administrative and coordinate comparisons into Table 2, removes the radar chart, redesigns architecture and curation diagrams, and adds distribution maps and diagnostic displays. Some existing material is relocated, including the benchmark map and training-stage table. New Figure 9 also contains inconsistent ground-truth labels and reported errors.

improvement.justification: The component ablations, size-matched Introspection control, and Qwen3 transfer test strengthen evidence for MG-Geo beyond v2's training-stage comparison. Explicit distribution and benchmark-comparability qualifications also improve transparency. These benefits are partly offset by removing the human dialogue assessment, underspecifying the new automated judges, and introducing inconsistent qualitative evidence: Figure 9 pairs a Denmark ground truth with a Melbourne prediction and a 0.2406 km error. The net improvement is therefore limited.
